## Context

[ADR 0004](../learn/agentos/decisions/0004-github-content-architecture.md) (`learn/agentos/decisions/0004-github-content-architecture.md`, Accepted 2026-05-14) is the single-source authority for the on-disk shape of `resources/content/`. It was written for **one repository** and says so nowhere — the assumption is load-bearing and invisible, which is the condition under which it gets violated silently.

D#17846 proposes extracting GitHub content sync into a dedicated corpus repository serving multiple origins. Its §8.9 D1 makes logical identity the tuple **`(repoSlug, type, id)`**. ADR 0004 §3.2 states the index schema as `{type, id, version, chunkNumber, path}` — no origin field — and that schema is not documentation drift: it is exactly what `normalizeContentIndexEntry` produces today.

**The empirical anchor is already in the ADR.** §2.2.1 exists because ordinals computed against partial membership produced 2,015 stale index entries and 27 byte-divergent duplicate artifacts (#15130 / #15319, @neo-opus-grace's measurement). That precondition is the section this amendment most changes, and for the same reason it was written.

## The Problem

Three facts, measured, that the current ADR cannot express:

1. **The index key collides across origins.** `ai/services/github-workflow/shared/contentIndex.mjs:224` — `indexKey()` returns `` `${type}:${id}` ``. Two origins' issue 1 produce one entry. @neo-gpt executed this against the real `updateContentIndex` (D#17846 §8.3b); I verified at source before folding it.
2. **Four enforcement sites, three of which bypass the key** (@neo-opus-grace's cycle, `DC_kwDODSospM4BGpNo`; each re-verified by me at Brain `407a89568c` and folded as D#17846 §8.4a). The factories at `contentIndex.mjs:131` / `:182` take no origin across 11 production construction sites in 4 files; `contentInventory.mjs:140` filters `entry.type` directly; `PullRequestSyncer.mjs:932` builds its own `Number(entry.id)` map.
3. 🔴 **The complete-membership precondition silently re-scopes, and this is the consequence neither peer packet names.** §2.2.1 requires `itemIndex` to be computed against a bucket's complete membership. Once origins share a tree, the bucket is `(repoSlug, type[, version])` — so a `buildContentInventory` scan rooted **above** the slugs computes membership across origins and yields *a different ordinal, not an approximate one*. That is §2.2.1's own failure mode, re-armed by the very change that adds the second origin, and it produces a valid-looking artifact in a plausible chunk. D#17846 §8.4 item 3 measured the sibling case for `findLogicalIdentityCollisions`; this is the same shape one layer down.

## The Architectural Reality

- `learn/agentos/decisions/0004-github-content-architecture.md` — the amendment target. §2.1 (on-disk shape), §2.2.1 (complete-membership precondition), §3.2 (index schema), §3.3 (syncer write-paths) are the sections that carry the single-repository assumption.
- The contract's implementation lives in the **Brain** (`ai/services/github-workflow/shared/contentIndex.mjs`, `contentInventory.mjs`, the three syncers); the **ADR lives in the engine**. This ticket amends the authority document only — no `ai/` code, no `AiConfig` touch.
- Authority for amending rather than superseding: [ADR 0005](../learn/agentos/decisions/0005-adr-at-graduation-for-ideation-sandbox.md) §2.3 — ADR-producing PRs follow the normal lifecycle, tickets may be filed pre-ADR-merge, and reviewers audit the updated ADR at the PR head rather than the previous accepted version.

## The Fix

Amend ADR 0004 in place. **Retain** the ordinal-100 rule, the complete-membership precondition, and ADR 0019's declared-configuration ownership; **introduce no second chunking primitive**. The amendment adds the origin dimension to what already exists:

- §2.1 — the tree gains a `<repoSlug>/` root above the families.
- §2.2.1 — the bucket against which complete membership is computed is stated as **per-origin**, with the above-the-slugs scan named as the re-armed failure.
- §3.2 — the schema gains `repoSlug`; logical identity is `(repoSlug, type, id)`; `path` is location and never an identity fallback.
- §3.3 — the custody cut: the producer writes only into the corpus repository.
- A migration boundary: **legacy unqualified input is accepted on read; every emitted row is qualified** (@neo-gpt's acceptance boundary — a round trip through a syncer is an emission, not a read).
- §5 anti-patterns — the two this work forecloses: an above-the-slugs membership scan, and reading read-tolerance as permission to publish partially qualified rows.

## The decided arm (§6.6 — matrix reduced at graduation)

**R — amend ADR 0004 in place.** One authority document keeps governing the on-disk shape; the origin dimension is added to the rules that already exist.

Both alternatives were carried with falsifiers while this ticket was provisional, and both are now closed:

- **A1 (a new ADR superseding 0004)** — rejected. ADR 0005 §2.4 bounds an ADR to decision, authority, retired primitives, sequencing and anti-patterns. A standalone successor would have to restate ordinal-100, complete membership and `prevent-reopen.yml` verbatim to stand on its own; that is a copy with one field added, so supersession is ceremony here.
- **A2 (leave 0004; let the Discussion body carry the contract)** — rejected, and its falsifier had **already fired** when it was written: authority spread across a Discussion body that took four author folds in a single day is precisely the multi-source drift ADR 0005 §1 exists to prevent.

R's own falsifier stays live and is now an acceptance criterion rather than a hypothetical: if a reader of the amended §2.2.1 cannot tell whether a pre-amendment ordinal is still valid, in-place amendment has destroyed the history the ADR anchors, and a dated supersession section is required instead. **AC-6 is that falsifier, armed.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the amendment is written into `learn/agentos/decisions/0004-github-content-architecture.md` itself, dated, with no second architecture document created.
- [ ] **AC-2** — §3.2's schema carries `repoSlug`, and logical identity is stated as the tuple `(repoSlug, type, id)` across upsert, lookup, removal, integrity and serialization.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `path` is stated to be location only, and **never** an identity fallback. The §8.3b collision (two origins' issue 1 normalizing to one entry) is named as the measured reason.
- [ ] **AC-4** — §3.3 carries the custody cut: the producer writes only into the corpus repository.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the migration boundary is stated in the direction @neo-gpt's acceptance boundary requires: **legacy unqualified input is accepted on read; every emitted row is qualified**, with a round trip through a syncer named explicitly as an emission and not a read. No partially qualified publication and no permanent second format are authorized.
- [ ] **AC-6** — §2.2.1 states the complete-membership bucket as **per-origin**, names the above-the-slugs scan as the re-armed failure, **and** says in terms whether a pre-amendment ordinal remains valid. *(This is R's own falsifier: if the answer cannot be written, R was the wrong arm and a dated supersession section is required instead.)*
- [ ] **AC-7** — §5 gains the two anti-patterns this work forecloses: an above-the-slugs membership scan, and reading read-tolerance as permission to publish partially qualified rows.
- [ ] **AC-8** — ordinal-100, the complete-membership precondition and ADR 0019's declared-configuration ownership are **retained verbatim in force**; the diff introduces no second chunking primitive. ADR 0019 is re-read before its clause is written, per §critical_gates 10.
- [ ] **AC-9** — the three `revalidationTrigger` reads in the graduation ledger are re-run at authoring time and their results stated in the PR body. D#17846's body has moved four times in one day; this AC is the guard against writing the amendment from a stale summary.

## Out of Scope

- Every consumer cutover (KB, Portal/Pages, FM, `LocalFileService`, `IssueIngestor`) — D#17846 §8.9 D4 gates each separately.
- The Brain-side implementation of the contract. This ticket amends the authority document; the code is a separate leaf.
- Archive dissolution and release-note relocation — ruled out of the producer cut in D#17846 §8.3a.
- ADR 0019 itself. Its declared-configuration ownership is retained, not revisited.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not add a second chunking primitive.** ADR 0004 §1.1 records the operator correction that produced the universal rule: *"consistency is key. same for all."* An origin dimension is a new bucket key, not a new chunking scheme.
- ⛔ **Do not let `path` become an identity fallback.** A `<repoSlug>/` prefix distinguishes files on disk and does not survive normalization — that is precisely how §8.3b's collision was missed.
- ⛔ **Do not write the amendment from this ticket's summary of D#17846.** The Discussion moved four times on 2026-09-19; re-read §8.4a and §8.9 at authoring time.
